question: Who has been appointed as the new Chief of the Special Protection Group (SPG) by the centre in November 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alok Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alok Sharma**, a senior Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, was appointed as the new Chief of the Special Protection Group (SPG) by the Indian government in November 2023.
 
• The SPG is tasked with providing proximate security to the Prime Minister of India, former Prime Ministers, and their immediate families.
 
• Alok Sharma has extensive experience in security and intelligence operations, making him an ideal candidate for this crucial position.
 
• The appointment follows the established protocol for selecting senior officers with proven track records of service excellence in high-stakes security roles.
 
• His leadership is expected to further enhance the operational efficiency and strategic capabilities of the SPG.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Special Protection Group (SPG)**:

 
 
• Established in 1988, the SPG is an elite force created under the Special Protection Group Act to ensure the security of India's top leaders.
 
• It provides 24/7 security cover to the Prime Minister, former Prime Ministers, and their immediate family members as per the Act's provisions.
 
• The SPG operates under the Cabinet Secretariat of India and is trained in advanced security protocols, counter-terrorism, and modern surveillance techniques.
 
 
 
• **Selection of SPG Chief**:
 
 
• The SPG Chief is typically a senior IPS officer with exemplary service credentials in intelligence and security operations.
 
• The appointment is made by the central government, ensuring the officer has the expertise to handle the complexities of high-profile security arrangements.
 
 
 
• **Key Responsibilities of SPG**:
 
 
• Protecting the Prime Minister, including during domestic and international visits.
 
• Ensuring comprehensive threat assessment and neutralizing potential risks.
 
• Maintaining coordination with state police forces and intelligence agencies for seamless operations.
 
 
 
• **Recent Reforms in SPG**:
 
 
• The SPG Act was amended in 2019 to restrict its protection to only the current Prime Minister and their immediate family residing with them.
 
• This reform aimed to streamline the force's operations and focus its resources on the nation's highest executive authority.
